pairs.question: O quis te in terris loquitur iucundior uno?
pairs.answer: Clio nam certe candida non loquitur.
pairs.derivation: Verse; stripped poem-number marker 'IV.' and the dangling inline verse number '10'. Line 9 is a genuine interrogative ('who on earth speaks more pleasantly than you alone?') and line 10 answers it ('for surely not even fair Clio speaks [more pleasantly]', i.e. no one does). Kept verbatim and contiguous; 'O' is the speaker's own interjection. Did not extend forward into 'Quare illud satis est...' (line 11), which turns to a new conclusion, nor back into the preceding rhetorical questions (lines 4, 8) which receive no answer.
